items.title: 1Password Find Item
items.text: 1Password Find Item is a command-line tool for searching item fields across your 1Password vaults.

items.title: Getting started
items.text:
1Password Find Item searches field values, including password and other secret fields, without printing the matched values. It uses the official 1Password SDK and desktop-app authentication.

  1. Install the CLI.
  2. Configure account authentication.
  3. Search your items.

See the API reference for the package's Python API.

items.title: Account authentication
items.text:
The CLI authenticates through the 1Password desktop app using the official 1Password SDK. Install the desktop app, sign in, and unlock it before searching. The CLI does not ask for or store your account password, Secret Key, or a service-account token.

You must provide the account name with --account-name or the OP_ACCOUNT_NAME environment variable. Use the email address for your account or the account UUID shown by:

op account list --format json

Pass the account name on a single invocation:

op-find-item --account-name "name@example.com" example

Or set the environment variable for the current shell:

export OP_ACCOUNT_NAME="name@example.com"
op-find-item example

Avoid putting credentials in scripts or source control. The account name identifies the account; authentication and access are still handled by the unlocked desktop app.

items.title: Sharing links
items.text:
By default, results show the vault, item, and matching field names, not the matched field values. This permits searching password and other secret fields without printing those values in the results.

The optional --include-link creates a one-time share link for each matching item. Anyone who obtains a link can view the shared item once; unused links expire after one hour. Use this option only when you intend to share, and treat output containing links as sensitive.

items.title: Installation
items.text: The CLI requires Python 3.11 or newer and the 1Password desktop app.

items.title: Install as a standalone command
items.text:
The recommended installation uses uv:

uv tool install op-find-item

Alternatively, install with pipx:

pipx install op-find-item

You can also install it into the active Python environment with pip:

python -m pip install op-find-item

Confirm installation:

op-find-item --help

items.title: Install from source
items.text:
Clone the GitHub repository, then install the project and its development dependencies:

git clone https://github.com/sbfeinstein/op-find-item.git
cd op-find-item
uv sync

Run the CLI from the checkout with:

uv run op-find-item --help

items.title: Usage
items.text: Search terms are matched as literal substrings of field values. The default is case-sensitive. Searches include all fields, including password and other secret fields; result output does not include the matched values.

items.title: Basic searches
items.text:
# Search all vaults and fields for the case-sensitive term "github"
op-find-item github

# Match regardless of letter case
op-find-item --ignore-case github

items.title: Limit the search
items.text:
Repeat --vault and --field to include multiple names. Names are matched as provided:

op-find-item --vault Personal --vault Work --field username --field password github

items.title: JSON output and sharing links
items.text:
JSON output is useful for scripting. It includes the vault, item, field name, and field type, but not the field value:

op-find-item --output-format json --ignore-case github

Adding --include-link creates one-time share links to matching items. These links grant access to anyone who has them; read the authentication and sharing guidance before using this option.

op-find-item --output-format json --include-link github

Run op-find-item --help for all options and examples.
